summary: The geometry meets the brief: lengths 44/25/22 mm, ranges 0-80/0-80/0-70 with every sweep and the curl clear, both channels open at 1.91 mm (min 1.5) after the flat-floor change, hard stops proven, real catalog shoulder-screw pivots, no supports, 29.3 g of 40. It fails on strength, which the paused FEA no longer covers. The last measured distal_fea_extensor was 25.01 MPa against 24 allowed, but DESIGN s8 still claims 20.0. The pivot shoulder screws work in single shear, and nothing (no engine check, no hand calc) checks their M3 thread neck. A hand calc puts it at or past yield for plain steel under the designer's own 222 N line case. Neither fix needs a redesign: a step-thickness change plus honest numbers on the distal, and a screw grade (or a derated line load) on the pivots.

findings.issue: All three pivots (mcp in base, pip in proximal, dip in middle; fingerlib.PIN = motion.shoulder_4_m3). The joints are single-shear laps. The child band bears on the shoulder centred 0.2 + 7.6/2 = 4.0 mm from the shoulder end, and the shoulder end sits on the insert mouth, so the M3 thread neck is a short cantilever. At the designer's own 222 N line case: M = 222 x 4.0 = 888 N mm on the M3 minor section (d3 2.387, Z = pi d3^3/32 = 1.34 mm3), which gives up to 665 MPa. If the contact moves toward the near end of the band, it is still about 330 MPa (lever 2 mm). The preload at 0.2-0.3 N m only carries roughly 300 N mm before the shoulder face lifts. The catalog entry says only 'zinc-plated steel' with no grade. Typical plain-steel grades yield at about 340-640 MPa, so the screw may bend at the load the design says it is rated for, and 222 N is also about what a 10 N fingertip at straight needs (19.4 F). No engine check covers this: kerf/pins.py proves length and engagement only, and the engine's pin moment goes onto the plastic, not the screw. The same moment loads the 4.6 x 5.7 mm insert in PETG. A rigid-pile estimate gives about 70 MPa bearing at the insert mouth (8.5 MPa x (4 + 6 x 4.0/5.7)), which matches the 59-62 MPa surface peaks the earlier FEA showed at the bores. p99.9 hides this, and with FEA paused nothing re-checks it. Expect the pivots to take a set and develop play under hard pulls.
findings.fix: Pick a shoulder screw with a known grade and record it in the catalog with its source: an alloy-steel class 12.9 4 mm shoulder, M3 (e.g. the Accu SSH-M3-8 already cited in the entry; yield about 1080 MPa, which gives SF about 1.6-3 on the estimate above). Its 6 x 3 socket head changes the 1.8 mm head-proud figure, so re-check the neighbour-finger room. Add the thread-neck bending and insert-mouth bearing hand checks to DESIGN s8. If the low slotted head must stay, derate instead: state the line tension the plain-steel neck allows (about 100 N for sigma <= 300 MPa at the 4 mm lever) and the fingertip force that gives. Fill the s8 rows from the next un-paused FEA run.

findings.issue: Washer line stops. The last FEA run before the pause gave distal_fea_extensor = 25.01 MPa p99.9 against 24.0 allowed (FAIL), peaking at [9.0, 0, 3.2] on the palmar wall of the extensor channel's last, 40 deg descending leg just behind the washer step. distal_fea_flexor was 23.89 (0.5 % margin). Both runs were on the detail-pass geometry. The dd32cf9 flat floor only adds material at y = +/-0.95 on the bed side and cannot reach that y = 0 site, so the fail very probably still stands. DESIGN s8 still lists 20.0 and 18.5 MPa and calls the FEA 'the proof', which overstates what has been proven. The mechanism is visible in the code. The 12 MPa nominal washer bearing (s7) flows around the 2.2 mm channel end only stop_step = 1.5 mm behind the seat. The oblique last leg (7.5, 6.15) -> (10, 4.0) puts the channel wall across that flow. The taut extensor also wraps the convex corner at x 7.5 at the same spot, a load the FEA does not model. The report now shows the case as PAUSED/ok. Strength here is unproven, and the last evidence is a fail.
findings.fix: Move the channel end away from the seat: stop_step 1.5 -> 2.0 (inside its declared range) and raise ext_stop_z toward 4.4 so the last leg is flatter and the line kink at the hole entry is smaller. Round the convex corner where the descending leg leaves the 6.15 run (r >= 1 mm in the XZ plane). Re-check flexor_open/extensor_open and the slot skins with `kerf req`. In DESIGN s8, replace the stale numbers with the last measured values, mark both distal cases 'PAUSED - unproven, last run 25.0 / 23.9', and re-run both cases first when stress simulation resumes.

findings.issue: The report's '4 sharp inside corners' on middle and '2' on distal come from an engine frame bug, not missing design work. kerf/pipeline.py:214 calls edges.split_kept on edges.sharp_inside(it.shape) after the joint solve has moved the shape into the assembly frame, while ctx.keep_sharp (kerf/ctx.py:104) stores part-frame points. The middle's [44.1, -3.7, 9.0] and [68.8, -3.7, 9.0] are part-frame x 0.1 / 24.8, exactly the corners middle.py's keep lambda declares. The [56.5/56.7, 1.9, ...] edges are channel roof apexes (y = 1.1 / sin 35 = 1.9), which fillet_inside declares 'faces down'. The distal's [69.1, 3.8, 9.0] and [77.8, -1.9, 5.1] are the same two kinds. Base and proximal sit at the assembly origin, so they match by coincidence. Any project with a moved child part gets false sharp-corner warnings.
findings.fix: In _print_checks, map the kerf_sharp_ok points through it.shape.location before split_kept (or compute sharp_inside on the unmoved shape). Check kerf_sites the same way. Add a test with a child part offset from the origin.

findings.issue: Stale and broken evidence in the review pack. Every out/renders/fea_*.png is from Oct 31 23:45, before the detail pass, the flat floor and the pause. The proximal ones show a broken solve (proximal_fea p99.9 1824.77 MPa for a 15 N load; proximal_fea_line 4793 MPa), which fits the non-manifold proximal mesh that dd32cf9 fixed. The brief's graded requirement proximal_fea therefore has no valid result on the current geometry. By hand it is trivial (660 N mm / Z about 800 mm3 = 0.8 MPa, bearing 0.5 MPa), so the risk is low, but it is unproven. Also, out/review/catalog.json is empty ('0 entries') although catalog_deps.json lists 12 entries.
findings.fix: Have the build or review-pack delete or label FEA renders whose requirement is NOT RUN (PAUSED), and fill review/catalog.json from catalog_deps.json. When stress resumes, run proximal_fea and proximal_fea_line first and confirm the mesh is one connected watertight body.

findings.issue: DESIGN.md is stale in several places since the detail pass and dd32cf9. s7 says the clear diameter across a joint is '0.4 gap + 2 x 0.9 groove = 2.2 mm' and does not describe the flat channel floor (FLOOR = 30 deg, bed-side groove now 0.75 mm deep, probe 1.91 mm). s10 says middle wall p2 >= 1.27 (now 1.40). s8b says masses 7.2/10.2/6.2 and total 28.9 g (now 7.4/10.4/6.3, 29.3 g). s8a says the distal is '18 mm deep knuckle tapering to the fingertip pad', but distal.py is a constant 18 mm rectangle ending in an R9 half-round with no taper. No section says the six fea_static results are PAUSED and strength is unproven.
findings.fix: Update s7 (flat floor, 1.91 mm), s8/s8a/s8b/s10 to the current report, and add one line in s8 stating the paused status.

findings.issue: Tendon exits. Both lines leave the base's back face through plain 2.2 mm holes with a sharp edge. There is no flare and no seat for a Bowden sheath, although the actuator sits behind and the line will rarely leave exactly along X. Under 100-200 N, a braid pulled at an angle over a square PETG edge saws a slot in it and frays. This is the only place on the finger where the line slides over a fixed edge at full load.
findings.fix: Give each exit a 1-1.5 mm radius bell-mouth (cove the channel end), or a counterbore for a PTFE Bowden sheath (e.g. 2.0-2.5 mm OD x 5 mm) so the sheath carries the angle. Note it in DESIGN s7 and in the base's assembly_note.

findings.issue: Concept lever left unused. The flexor runs 4.7 mm palmar of the axes while the extensor uses 6.15 mm (the same 1.75 mm skin would allow the flexor at about -6.15). The required line tension, and with it every pivot load (finding 1) and the distal stop load (finding 2), scales with 1/arm. At 6.15 the straight-finger ratio drops from 19.4 F to about 14.8 F, 24 % less for the same fingertip force. The C-6 insert-wall constraint gets easier, not harder, because the chord only moves further from the axis.
findings.fix: Try FLEX about 6.0 with flexor crown or exit points like the extensor's. Re-run the sweeps, channel_clear and the 1.6 mm insert-wall check. If it holds, update DESIGN s7's tip-force rating (about 14-15 N at a straight tip for 222 N).

findings.issue: Proportions and craft. All four parts are the same 15.6 x 18 mm box section with full-round ends. The fingertip is 18 mm deep, while an adult index distal is about 12-14 mm (the brief asks for 'like a real index finger'). The mid-shafts carry about 1 MPa at the brief's 15 N case, so the uniform box is not derived from the load except at the knuckle bands. The 10-deg stepped swept grooves leave a serrated fan of ridges on every knuckle rim (visible in all part sheets). That is disclosed in s10 as a possible rub point for a 0.8 mm line. Everything else is purposeful: the lugs, the bosses, the chamfers and the pointed roofs all have a stated job.
findings.fix: Optional, on the next geometry pass: taper the distal past the stop slots toward about 14 mm at the tip (the slots need about 1.7 mm of skin at z -6.5 / +6.7, so the taper starts at x about 16). Consider 5-deg STEP only where the ridges face the line (rim, r > 8). Spec the 0.5-0.6 mm braid in the BOM row rather than 0.5-0.8.
